thesis: Today the pack finally gives me a thread with enough corroboration to spend the cash I have been sitting on since 9/1, and it is an inflation-and-rates thread rather than an AI one. Four separate items point the same way: crude is pushing toward 100 dollars on the Mideast flare-up and explicitly fanning inflation fears, the US 30-year fixed mortgage rate has climbed to its highest since June 2025, the bond market sell-off is now showing up in earnings reports, and Turkey lifted its inflation forecast to 28.4% citing the same conflict. That is a price level, a rate level, an earnings channel and a foreign inflation print, from four directions, and it sits on top of the U.S.-Iran escalation I acted on yesterday. I have to address my own record here, because I round-tripped XOM twice in June and then said I would not re-enter energy without something with more shelf life than a one-line oil headline. I think this clears that bar and I want to be precise about why: June was a single directional sentence about oil rising on strikes, which reversed the next session on a single sentence about a deal. Today is a crude level with a named transmission channel into inflation, confirmed by three other items across two packs. If I refuse this because I was wrong twice on a weaker version of it, I am managing my own embarrassment rather than the book. So I open a 12 dollar XOM sleeve, roughly 10% of equity, funded entirely from cash rather than by selling tech. The funding choice matters. Rising long rates are the most direct valuation headwind to what I own, since QQQ, NVDA and XLK are all long-duration growth, so the point of this trade is to put a non-tech leg with inflation beta against that exposure, not to shrink my market exposure further. I already cut NVDA yesterday on the escalation, and trimming it again the day after on the same continuing theme would be serial de-risking into a falling tape rather than a decision. NVDA stays near 39% of equity, comfortably inside the 50% cap. The rest of the pack does not move me: Bloom Energy's S&P 500 addition, the FLEX 4.4 billion dollar AI power bet, the NextEra-Dominion merger vote and Eni's Uruguay blocks are all real facts about companies outside my 20 symbols, and the Dell-versus-HPE and Micron-versus-Sandisk pieces are comparison listicles. After fills, cash falls to roughly 11 dollars, about 9% of equity against my 5% floor, the book holds 4 of 8 positions, and no name approaches the cap under any plausible open.
